sync.prompt: Choose which Salesforce objects to sync
sync.sync_objects_note: No sync.objects yet, on purpose. The only listing node this app has is salesforce-query_records-1, which takes a SOQL statement, and a SOQL statement for a picked object type is built by joining strings - which the four value-expression operators cannot do. The engine would need a salesforce-list_records-1 node taking { object_type, since, cursor } and writing its own SOQL inside execute.ts. That node is the whole work; the recipe after it is ten lines.

quirks.sync_stores_the_api_name: A picked object is stored as its API name — Account, Roast_Batch__c — because that is what a SOQL FROM clause takes, so a crawler reading sync_scope can query with the id it saved. salesforce-list_object_types-1 hides the share, history, feed and change-event shadows.
quirks.base_url_is_a_template: Salesforce has no shared API host. The token response returns instance_url (https://acme.my.salesforce.com) beside the access token, and that host is where every API call goes. base_url above is the LOGIN host: correct for /services/oauth2/authorize, /services/oauth2/token, and the app's catalog request origin. The call host is resolved per connection in salesforce_api.ts.
quirks.connection_must_carry_instance_url: Whatever completes the OAuth exchange must store instance_url from the token response on the connection. Without it every node in this app fails with a named error instead of calling the login host.
quirks.api_version: v61.0, pinned per node version. A newer Salesforce API version is a new v{n}/ folder, never an edit to an existing one.
quirks.rate_limits: Salesforce meters a daily org quota (tens of thousands of calls), not a per-minute one, and caps concurrent long-running requests at 25. These numbers keep one connection under both while still filling a 200-record composite batch quickly.
quirks.sandboxes_not_supported: Sandbox orgs authenticate at test.salesforce.com. This app targets production orgs; a sandbox app is a separate app_key.
